items.exampleCN: 那匹马乌黑发亮。

definition_en: the land beside the sea, or to move without much power, especially downhill or through a task
core_image: 公路一侧是白房子，另一侧是不断拍岸的海水
scene: 公路一侧是低矮的白房子，另一侧是不断拍岸的海水。The road follows the coast for twenty miles.
sceneCN: 这里 coast 指「海岸」（第 1 个义项：临海的那片陆地）；句意是这条路沿着海岸延伸二十英里。

senses.title: Land beside the sea
senses.definition: the land that runs along the edge of the sea
senses.definitionCN: 沿着海边延伸的那片陆地
senses.example: We drove along the coast at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落时我们沿着海岸开车。
senses.why: The Latin word meant a rib or a side, and the sea's side of the land took that name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁原词指肋骨或侧面，陆地的临海一面便用了这个名字。

senses.title: Move without power
senses.definition: to move forward by momentum alone, without using power
senses.definitionCN: 仅凭惯性向前移动，不施加动力
senses.example: The bike coasted down the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车顺着山坡滑下去。
senses.why: A ship coasts when it keeps moving with no sail or oar, and wheels borrowed the same motion.
senses.whyCN: 船在不用帆桨时仍前行叫 coast，车轮也借用了这种运动。

senses.title: Get through with little effort
senses.definition: to succeed or finish with very little effort
senses.definitionCN: 几乎不费力气就完成或通过
senses.example: He coasted through the final test.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻松通过了期末测验。
senses.why: Moving without power became a picture of working without effort.
senses.whyCN: 不施动力地前进成了不费力气做事的比喻。

intro.en: Coast comes from the Latin word for a rib or a side, and then the side of the land.
intro.cn: coast 出自拉丁语中表示肋骨或侧面的词，后指陆地的侧边。

items.en: Costa meant a rib or the side of a body.
items.cn: costa 指肋骨或身体的一侧。

items.en: Coste meant a side or an edge.
items.cn: coste 指侧面或边缘。

items.en: Coast named the edge of the land beside the sea.
items.cn: coast 指陆地临海的一边。

items.en: The verb sense of moving without power appeared in sailing.
items.cn: 不施动力的动词义在航海中出现。

items.en: The verb now also means to get through a task easily.
items.cn: 这个动词如今还指轻松完成一项任务。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape, while the meaning group names the edge of the sea.
note.cn: 形近组收形状接近的词，近义组列出海边地带。

entries.definition: the amount of money needed to buy something
entries.definitionCN: 购买某物所需的钱

entries.definition: bread browned by heat
entries.definitionCN: 加热烤成棕色的面包

entries.definition: a small mat for a glass, or a ship along the coast
entries.definitionCN: 垫杯子的小垫，或沿海航行的船

entries.definition: the land along the edge of a sea or a lake
entries.definitionCN: 海或湖边缘的陆地

entries.definition: the area beside the sea where people go on holiday
entries.definitionCN: 人们度假去的海边地区

entries.definition: an area of sand or stones beside the sea
entries.definitionCN: 海边的沙地或石滩

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the rib picture, the seaside road and the bike that rolls downhill.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从肋骨意象、海边公路和下坡滑行的自行车入手。

normal.en: The Latin costa meant a rib, and the coast is the rib of the land.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 costa 指肋骨，而海岸就是陆地的肋骨。

normal.en: Coast and cost differ by one letter; the coast costs nothing to look at.
normal.cn: coast 与 cost 只差一个字母，而看海不花钱。

normal.en: Coastline joins coast and line, and the line is drawn on a map.
normal.cn: coastline 由 coast 与 line 合成，那条线画在地图上。

normal.en: A bike coasts downhill with the pedals still.
normal.cn: 自行车下坡滑行时脚踏板是不动的。

normal.en: Coasting through an exam means letting momentum carry you.
normal.cn: coasting through an exam 就是靠惯性过关。

abstract.en: Picture a white road with sea on one side and low houses on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一条白路，一边是海，一边是矮房。

abstract.en: Picture a bicycle with both feet off the pedals on a slope.
abstract.cn: 想象自行车下坡，双脚离开脚踏板。

abstract.en: Picture a ship drifting with its sails down.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船落下帆顺水漂。

examples.en: They walked along the coast until the light failed.
examples.cn: 他们沿着海岸一直走到天色暗下来。

examples.en: The van coasted into the last stretch of road.
examples.cn: 货车滑行进入最后一段路。

examples.en: She coasted through the first year of the course.
examples.cn: 她轻轻松松读完了这门课的第一年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 coast 记成「陆地的肋骨」：海的边缘像一排肋骨，船沿它轻轻滑过。

root: 源自拉丁语 costa（肋骨、侧面），经古法语 coste 进入英语，本义是陆地的侧边，即海岸。

sensesIntro.en: From the side of the land to moving without power, and then to effort-free success.
sensesIntro.cn: 从陆地的侧边，到不施动力地移动，再到毫不费力的成功。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the long edge where land meets water.
core.cn: 核心意象：陆地与海水相接的那条长边。

branches.en: The land sense is the everyday core of the word.
branches.cn: 陆地义是这个词的日常核心。

branches.en: The moving sense comes from ships that drift without power.
branches.cn: 移动义来自不施动力漂行的船。

branches.en: Effortless work borrows the picture of drifting forward.
branches.cn: 不费力的做事借用了顺势前行的画面。

branches.en: The shore and the drifting ship share one word in seafaring.
branches.cn: 海岸与漂行的船在航海语里共用一词。

branches.en: Both senses describe movement with no engine behind it.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述没有动力推动的移动。

intro.en: The stem builds adjectives, nouns and a large set of compounds about the sea edge.
intro.cn: 这个词干构成形容词、名词以及大量关于海边的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin costa, a rib or a side, which became French coste.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 costa（肋骨、侧面），后成法语 coste。

items.meaning: more than one stretch of seashore
items.example: Both coasts have mild winters.
items.exampleCN: 两岸的冬天都很温和。

items.meaning: relating to the land beside the sea
items.example: Coastal towns depend on fishing.
items.exampleCN: 沿海城镇依靠捕鱼。

items.meaning: the outline of the coast
items.example: The coastline is broken by many bays.
items.exampleCN: 海岸线被许多海湾断开。

items.meaning: a ship that sails along the coast, or a small mat
items.example: A coaster moved slowly into the harbour.
items.exampleCN: 一艘沿海船慢慢驶入港口。

items.meaning: the land near the coast
items.example: The coastland is flat and wet.
items.exampleCN: 这片沿海地区平坦而潮湿。

items.meaning: a road that follows the coast
items.example: The coast road was closed by snow.
items.exampleCN: 沿海公路因雪封闭。

items.meaning: the service that protects people at sea
items.example: The coast guard answered the call.
items.exampleCN: 海岸警卫队回应了呼救。

items.meaning: going from one coast to the other
items.example: They made a coast-to-coast journey.
items.exampleCN: 他们做了一次横贯全国的旅行。

latinEntries.example: Costa gave French coste and English coast.
latinEntries.exampleCN: costa 衍生出法语 coste 与英语 coast。

definition_en: a piece of outer clothing with sleeves, a layer of paint or other material covering a surface, or to cover something with such a layer
core_image: 出门迎寒前披上肩头的那件厚外套
scene: 清早的风很冷，他抓起门边的大衣往身上套。He buttoned his coat and walked out into the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 coat 指「外套」（第 1 个义项：有袖子的外衣）；句意是他扣好外套，走进了雨中。

senses.title: An outer garment
senses.definition: a piece of clothing with sleeves that you wear over other clothes to keep warm
senses.definitionCN: 穿在其他衣服外面、有袖子用来保暖的衣物
senses.example: Hang your coat behind the door.
senses.exampleCN: 把你的外套挂在门后。
senses.why: The word first named a long outer robe, and warmth is still its first job.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指长外袍，保暖至今仍是它的首要用途。

senses.title: A covering layer
senses.definition: a layer of paint or other material spread over a surface
senses.definitionCN: 涂在表面上的一层油漆或其他材料
senses.example: The wall needs two coats of white paint.
senses.exampleCN: 这面墙需要刷两层白漆。
senses.why: A layer of paint sits on a wall the way a coat sits on a body.
senses.whyCN: 一层漆盖在墙上，就像外套披在身上。

senses.title: To cover a surface
senses.definition: to cover something with a thin layer of a substance
senses.definitionCN: 用薄薄一层物质盖住某物
senses.example: Dust coated every shelf in the empty room.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘盖满了空房间里的每个架子。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to give a surface its own coat.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词：给表面穿上一层外套。

intro.en: Coat comes through Old French from a late Latin word for a long outer tunic.
intro.cn: coat 经古法语上溯到晚期拉丁语，原指长外袍。

items.en: Cotta named a coarse outer garment.
items.cn: cotta 指一种粗糙的外衣。

items.en: Old French cote kept the sense of a long robe.
items.cn: 古法语 cote 保留了长袍之义。

items.en: English coat first meant a long gown worn outdoors.
items.cn: 英语 coat 最初指在户外穿的长袍。

items.en: Tailors narrowed it to the everyday outer garment for the upper body.
items.cn: 裁缝把它收窄为日常的上身外套。

items.en: Painters and scientists borrowed it for any covering layer.
items.cn: 画家和科学家又借它指任何覆盖层。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that echo the spelling of coat, while the meaning group names garments and layers.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写与 coat 相近的短词，近义组列出衣物与覆盖层。

entries.definition: to have a particular price
entries.definitionCN: 价格为；花费

entries.definition: a bus for long journeys or a person who trains others
entries.definitionCN: 长途客车；教练

entries.definition: a place where legal cases are heard
entries.definitionCN: 审理案件的法庭

entries.definition: a short coat that covers the top half of the body
entries.definitionCN: 夹克；短外套

entries.definition: a long warm coat worn over other clothes
entries.definitionCN: 穿在其他衣服外面的暖和长大衣

entries.definition: a thickness of material covering a surface
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖在表面上的一层物质

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the warm garment, then move to the thin layer on a wall and the act of covering.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从保暖的外衣出发，再走到墙上的薄层与覆盖的动作。

normal.en: A coat goes over everything else, just as the word covers clothes, paint and dust.
normal.cn: 外套穿在所有衣服外面，这个词也像外衣一样盖住衣物、油漆和灰尘。

normal.en: The same spelling serves the noun and the verb, so one picture does two jobs.
normal.cn: 名词和动词拼写相同，一幅画面就承担了两种用法。

normal.en: Remember the phrase a coat of paint and the covering sense becomes easy.
normal.cn: 记住「一层油漆」这个说法，覆盖义就很容易。

normal.en: Coated and coating keep the same idea of a layer.
normal.cn: coated 与 coating 保留的仍是那一层的意象。

normal.en: A coat has sleeves, so it is warmer and longer than a jacket.
normal.cn: 外套有袖子，所以比夹克更暖也更长。

abstract.en: Picture a hall stand by the door, heavy with winter coats.
abstract.cn: 想象门边的衣帽架，挂满了厚重的冬衣。

abstract.en: Picture a painter laying one smooth white coat on a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象油漆工在墙上刷上平滑的一层白漆。

abstract.en: Picture dust settling until every shelf wears a grey coat.
abstract.cn: 想象灰尘落下，直到每个架子都披上一层灰。

examples.en: He took off his wet coat and hung it by the fire.
examples.cn: 他脱下湿外套，挂在炉火旁。

examples.en: The floor was coated with a thin layer of dust.
examples.cn: 地板上覆着薄薄一层灰。

examples.en: You will need three coats of paint for a deep colour.
examples.cn: 要得到浓郁的颜色，你需要刷三遍漆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 coat 记成出门必穿的那件外套：一件衣服护住全身，一层漆护住墙面。

root: 经古法语 cote 上溯拉丁语 cotta，本指粗糙的长外衣，后收窄为上身外套，又引申为覆盖的一层。

sensesIntro.en: From the warm garment on your back to the thin layer on a wall, and then to the act of covering.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身上的暖衣，到墙上的薄层，再到覆盖的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick coat pulled on before stepping into the cold.
core.cn: 核心意象：出门迎寒前披上的那件厚外套。

branches.en: The garment sense is the oldest and still the everyday one.
branches.cn: 衣物义最古老，也是今天的日常义。

branches.en: A layer of paint lies on a wall like a coat on a body.
branches.cn: 一层漆盖在墙上，如外套披在身上。

branches.en: The verb simply gives a surface its own coat.
branches.cn: 动词义就是给表面穿上一层外衣。

branches.en: Clothing and covering share one image of something laid over.
branches.cn: 衣物与覆盖共享同一个盖在上面的意象。

branches.en: Paint and dust both arrive as thin coats.
branches.cn: 油漆与灰尘都是以薄薄一层到来的。

intro.en: Coat is a free base, so its family grows with endings and with compounds from daily life.
intro.cn: coat 是自由词基，家族靠词尾与日常复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestor cotta named a rough garment, not a layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语祖词 cotta 指粗糙衣物，并不指层。

items.meaning: more than one coat, or he covers a surface
items.example: Two coats hung by the door.
items.exampleCN: 门边挂着两件外套。

items.meaning: covered something with a layer
items.example: The pills are coated with sugar.
items.exampleCN: 这些药丸外面裹了糖衣。

items.meaning: the act of covering or the layer itself
items.example: A thin coating of ice covered the road.
items.exampleCN: 路面上结了一层薄冰。

items.meaning: without a coat
items.example: He ran out coatless into the snow.
items.exampleCN: 他没穿外套就冲进了雪里。

items.meaning: a long warm coat worn outdoors
items.example: Her overcoat reached her ankles.
items.exampleCN: 她的大衣长到脚踝。

items.meaning: a waterproof coat for wet weather
items.example: Take a raincoat because the sky is dark.
items.exampleCN: 带上雨衣，天色很暗。

items.meaning: the final layer of paint
items.example: The topcoat gives the wood its shine.
items.exampleCN: 面漆让木头有了光泽。

items.meaning: the first layer of paint
items.example: Apply an undercoat before the colour.
items.exampleCN: 上色前先刷一层底漆。

definition_en: a system of words or symbols used to represent information, a set of written rules or laws, or to write instructions for a computer
core_image: 把想法压缩成一串只有圈内人看得懂的符号
scene: 程序员盯着屏幕，把一段指令敲进编辑器。She wrote the code that runs the whole system.
sceneCN: 这里 code 指「代码」（第 1 个义项：计算机指令）；句意是她写下了运行整个系统的代码。

derivatives.zh: 编纂成法典；整理成系统

senses.title: Instructions for a computer
senses.definition: a set of instructions written for a computer program
senses.definitionCN: 为计算机程序编写的一组指令
senses.example: The code crashed when the file was too large.
senses.exampleCN: 文件太大时，这段代码崩溃了。
senses.why: A machine cannot read our words, so we hand it a private alphabet.
senses.whyCN: 机器读不懂人的语言，于是我们交给它一套私密字母表。

senses.title: A secret system of signs
senses.definition: a system of letters or symbols used to keep a message secret
senses.definitionCN: 用来保密信息的字母或符号系统
senses.example: The spy refused to give up the code.
senses.exampleCN: 那名间谍拒绝交出密码。
senses.why: Codes once kept messages safe from anyone without the key.
senses.whyCN: 密码曾让没有钥匙的人无法读懂信息。

senses.title: A set of written rules
senses.definition: a written set of laws or rules that govern behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 规范行为的一整套成文法律或规则
senses.example: Every member must follow the club's code.
senses.exampleCN: 每位成员都必须遵守俱乐部的准则。
senses.why: Law is also a code: signs arranged so that people can read what is allowed.
senses.whyCN: 法律也是一种代码：符号排好，让人读出什么被允许。

intro.en: Code traces back to Latin codex, the wooden tablet used for writing.
intro.cn: code 上溯拉丁语 codex，即用来书写的木板书板。

items.en: Codex meant a block of wood and then a tablet for writing.
items.cn: codex 本指一块木头，后指书写用的板。

items.en: A codex of laws held rules in one ordered book.
items.cn: 一部法典把规则收在一本有序的书里。

items.en: French code carried the legal sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 code 把法律义带进了英语。

items.en: The word spread from law to any organised set of signs.
items.cn: 这个词从法律扩展到任何有组织的符号系统。

items.en: Computing made code the everyday word for program text.
items.cn: 计算机让 code 成为程序文本的日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words that differ from code by one letter, while the meaning group covers secret writing and instruction sets.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 code 只差一两个字母的短词，近义组涉及密文与指令集。

entries.definition: a shape with a round base and a point
entries.definitionCN: 底面为圆、顶端带尖的形状

entries.definition: a long thin flexible rope
entries.definitionCN: 细长而有弹性的绳

entries.definition: to deal successfully with a hard situation
entries.definitionCN: 成功应付困难局面

entries.definition: a secret way of writing messages
entries.definitionCN: 书写密文的秘密方式

entries.definition: a set of instructions that makes a computer work
entries.definitionCN: 让计算机工作的一组指令

entries.definition: a rule made by a government for all people
entries.definitionCN: 政府为所有人制定的规则

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the wooden tablet, the secret letter and the lines a programmer types.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把木板书板、密信和程序员敲下的行行字符连在一起。

normal.en: A codex was a wooden tablet, so code begins with something written down.
normal.cn: codex 是木板书板，所以 code 的起点是写下来的东西。

normal.en: Laws were gathered into codes long before computers existed.
normal.cn: 早在计算机出现之前，法律就被汇编成法典。

normal.en: A code keeps a message closed to outsiders, like a locked box.
normal.cn: 密码把信息对局外人锁住，像一只上锁的箱子。

normal.en: Add the prefix de and decode means opening that box again.
normal.cn: 加上前缀 de，decode 就是把那只箱子重新打开。

normal.en: Code and decode sit at opposite ends of one message.
normal.cn: code 与 decode 位于同一条信息的两端。

abstract.en: Picture a monk copying laws onto a thick wooden tablet.
abstract.cn: 想象一位修士把法律条文抄到厚厚的木板上。

abstract.en: Picture a page of symbols that only one reader can unlock.
abstract.cn: 想象一页符号，只有一位读者能把它解开。

abstract.en: Picture green lines of text scrolling down a dark screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一行行绿色字符在暗屏上向下滚动。

examples.en: He spent the night fixing a bug in the code.
examples.cn: 他花了一整夜修复代码里的一个错误。

examples.en: The letter was written in a code that nobody could read.
examples.cn: 这封信是用没人能读懂的密码写的。

examples.en: The new code on dress makes the office more relaxed.
examples.cn: 新的着装准则让办公室氛围更轻松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 code 记成一本锁起来的符号册：翻开来是指令，锁起来是密码。

root: 源自拉丁语 codex（木板书板），经法语 code 进入英语，由成文法典扩展为符号系统与计算机指令。

sensesIntro.en: From a written tablet to a book of laws, then to hidden signs and machine instructions.
sensesIntro.cn: 从书写的木板，到成文法典，再到隐秘符号与机器指令。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a string of signs that carries meaning only to those who hold the key.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串只有持钥匙者才读得懂的符号。

branches.en: Machine code is the newest and most common sense today.
branches.cn: 机器代码是今天最新也最常用的义项。

branches.en: A cipher hides a message behind unfamiliar signs.
branches.cn: 密码用陌生的符号把信息藏起来。

branches.en: A code of law arranges rules in one readable order.
branches.cn: 法典把规则排成一个可读的顺序。

branches.en: Both senses rest on a fixed system of signs.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在固定的符号系统上。

branches.en: A programmer and a lawmaker both write codes that others must follow.
branches.cn: 程序员与立法者都在写别人必须遵循的代码。

intro.en: Code takes Latin prefixes easily, so its family is built on en-, de- and -ify.
intro.cn: code 很容易接拉丁前缀，家族靠 en-、de- 与 -ify 构建。

latinIntro.en: The base codex is Latin for a writing tablet, and codex still names an ancient book.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 codex 在拉丁语中指书写板，今天 codex 仍指古籍抄本。

items.meaning: more than one code, or he writes instructions
items.example: The two codes must match exactly.
items.exampleCN: 两套代码必须完全一致。

items.meaning: put into a code or written as a program
items.example: The message was coded before it was sent.
items.exampleCN: 这条信息在发送前已被加密。

items.meaning: the work of writing computer programs
items.example: Coding takes patience more than speed.
items.exampleCN: 编程更需要耐心而不是速度。

items.meaning: a person who writes computer code
items.example: She hired a coder for the new app.
items.exampleCN: 她为这款新应用请了一位程序员。

items.meaning: to change information into a code
items.example: The device encodes every call.
items.exampleCN: 这台设备把每通电话都编码。

items.meaning: to turn a code back into plain meaning
items.meaningCN: 把代码还原为明白的意思
items.example: They needed a key to decode the file.
items.exampleCN: 他们需要一把钥匙来解码这个文件。

items.meaning: to arrange rules into a clear system
items.meaningCN: 把规则整理成清晰的体系
items.example: The team codified its safety rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队把安全规则编纂成文。

items.meaning: the act of arranging rules into a code
items.example: The codification of the law took years.
items.exampleCN: 这部法律的编纂花了数年。

items.meaning: a pattern of lines read by a machine
items.example: The cashier scanned the barcode.
items.exampleCN: 收银员扫了条形码。

items.meaning: a group of letters and numbers used in an address
items.meaningCN: 地址中使用的邮政编码
items.example: Please write your postcode clearly.
items.exampleCN: 请把邮政编码写清楚。

latinEntries.meaning: a wooden tablet or a bound manuscript
latinEntries.example: The oldest codex in the library is under glass.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 馆中最古老的抄本放在玻璃罩下。

definition_en: a hot drink made from roasted beans, one cup of this drink, or the dark brown colour of it
core_image: 清晨桌上那杯冒着热气的深褐色液体
scene: 清晨的厨房里飘着烘焙豆子的香气。She poured herself a cup of coffee before work.
sceneCN: 这里 coffee 指「咖啡」（第 1 个义项：烘焙豆子煮成的热饮）；句意是她上班前给自己倒了一杯咖啡。

senses.title: The hot drink
senses.definition: a hot drink made by pouring water through roasted and ground beans
senses.definitionCN: 用热水冲过烘焙研磨的豆子制成的热饮
senses.example: He drinks his coffee without sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 他喝咖啡不加糖。
senses.why: The bean travelled from Ethiopia to Arabia before the drink reached Europe.
senses.whyCN: 这种豆子从埃塞俄比亚传到阿拉伯，饮料才进入欧洲。

senses.title: One cup of it
senses.definition: one cup or serving of this drink
senses.definitionCN: 一杯或一份这样的饮料
senses.example: Two coffees, please, one with milk.
senses.exampleCN: 请来两杯咖啡，一杯加奶。
senses.why: In cafés the drink became countable, ordered by the cup.
senses.whyCN: 在咖啡馆里，这种饮料按杯点，于是变成可数。

senses.title: The dark brown colour
senses.definition: a dark brown colour like that of coffee with milk
senses.definitionCN: 像加奶咖啡那样的深棕色
senses.example: She painted the walls a warm coffee colour.
senses.exampleCN: 她把墙刷成了温暖的咖啡色。
senses.why: The drink is so familiar that its colour needs no other name.
senses.whyCN: 这种饮料太常见，它的颜色不必另取名字。

intro.en: Coffee came from Arabic qahwa, probably by way of Turkish kahve.
intro.cn: coffee 出自阿拉伯语 qahwa，可能经土耳其语 kahve 传入。

items.en: Qahwa named the drink on the Arabian peninsula.
items.cn: qahwa 在阿拉伯半岛指这种饮料。

items.en: Turkish kahve carried the word westward.
items.cn: 土耳其语 kahve 把词带向西方。

items.en: Italian caffè named the new coffee houses of Venice.
items.cn: 意大利语 caffè 指威尼斯新开的咖啡馆。

items.en: Coffee shops spread quickly through London.
items.cn: 咖啡馆在伦敦迅速普及。

items.en: The word now also names the colour and the beans themselves.
items.cn: 这个词如今还指咖啡色与咖啡豆本身。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps words that rhyme with coffee, while the meaning group names drinks and the place that serves them.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 coffee 押韵的词，近义组列出饮品与售卖饮品的地方。

entries.definition: a sweet made by boiling sugar and butter
entries.definitionCN: 用糖和黄油熬成的太妃糖

entries.definition: a strong box used for keeping money
entries.definitionCN: 存放钱财的坚固箱子

entries.definition: to push air out of the throat with a sharp sound
entries.definitionCN: 喉咙猛地出声把气排出

entries.definition: strong coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans
entries.definitionCN: 用蒸汽冲过咖啡粉制成的浓咖啡

entries.definition: a small place that sells coffee and simple food
entries.definitionCN: 售卖咖啡与简单食物的小店

entries.definition: the substance in coffee that keeps people awake
entries.definitionCN: 咖啡中让人保持清醒的物质

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the smell of roasted beans, the morning cup and the brown colour on a wall.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从烘焙豆子的香气、清晨那杯咖啡和墙上的褐色入手。

normal.en: Coffee begins with the same two letters as the word cafe.
normal.cn: coffee 与 cafe 开头两个字母相同，可以一起记。

normal.en: Two f and two e sit in the middle, like two beans and two cups.
normal.cn: 中间两个 f 和两个 e，像两颗豆子和两只杯子。

normal.en: The drink is uncountable, but a cafe order makes it countable.
normal.cn: 这种饮料不可数，但在咖啡馆点单时就变得可数。

normal.en: Caffeine is the part of coffee that keeps you awake.
normal.cn: caffeine 就是咖啡里让人清醒的成分。

normal.en: The colour of coffee with milk gives the third sense without any new word.
normal.cn: 加奶咖啡的颜色直接带来第三个义项，不必另造新词。

abstract.en: Picture a warm cup on a windowsill while rain runs down the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象窗台上放着一杯热咖啡，雨水顺着玻璃流下。

abstract.en: Picture a small cafe where the counter smells of roasted beans.
abstract.cn: 想象一家小咖啡馆，柜台飘着烘焙豆子的香气。

abstract.en: Picture a coat in a deep coffee brown hanging beside a cream one.
abstract.cn: 想象一件深咖啡色的外套挂在米色外套旁边。

examples.en: The smell of coffee woke everyone in the house.
examples.cn: 咖啡的香气唤醒了屋里所有人。

examples.en: We ordered three coffees and sat by the window.
examples.cn: 我们点了三杯咖啡，坐在窗边。

examples.en: Her new coat is a soft coffee brown.
examples.cn: 她的新外套是一种柔和的咖啡色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 coffee 记成清晨那杯褐色热饮：闻着香，喝着苦，颜色还能染上墙。

root: 源自阿拉伯语 qahwa，经土耳其语 kahve 与意大利语 caffè 进入英语，由饮品引申为一杯咖啡与咖啡色。

sensesIntro.en: From the drink itself to a single cup of it, and then to the colour it lends to other things.
sensesIntro.cn: 从这种饮料本身，到一杯的分量，再到它借给别物的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dark hot liquid poured from a pot into a waiting cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：深色热液从壶里倒进一只等着的杯子。

branches.en: The drink is the sense that travellers carried across the world.
branches.cn: 饮品义是旅人带往世界各地的那个义项。

branches.en: A cafe turns the liquid into countable orders.
branches.cn: 咖啡馆把这种液体变成可数的一份份订单。

branches.en: The colour sense borrows the look of the drink directly.
branches.cn: 颜色义直接借用了饮料的外观。

branches.en: The same word covers the substance and one serving of it.
branches.cn: 同一个词既指这种物质，也指一份饮品。

branches.en: The drink supplies both a taste and a colour name.
branches.cn: 这种饮料同时提供了味道与颜色名称。

intro.en: Coffee compounds freely with everyday nouns, giving names for pots, houses and cups.
intro.cn: coffee 与日常名词自由复合，造出壶、屋、杯等名称。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the word arrived from Arabic through Turkish and Italian.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根，这个词从阿拉伯语经土耳其语和意大利语传来。

items.meaning: several cups or several kinds of coffee
items.example: The waiter brought two coffees.
items.exampleCN: 服务员端来两杯咖啡。

items.meaning: a place where people drink coffee and talk
items.meaningCN: 人们喝咖啡聊天的场所
items.example: The old coffeehouse hosted poets and traders.
items.exampleCN: 这家老咖啡馆曾接待诗人和商人。

items.meaning: a pot used for making or serving coffee
items.example: She rinsed the coffeepot before use.
items.exampleCN: 她用之前冲洗了咖啡壶。

items.meaning: a machine that makes coffee
items.example: The coffeemaker starts before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 咖啡机在天亮前就开始工作。

items.meaning: a small cup for drinking coffee
items.example: He stacked every coffee cup on the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 他把每只咖啡杯都摞在架子上。

items.meaning: the stimulant found in coffee and tea
items.meaningCN: 咖啡与茶中的提神物质
items.example: Too much caffeine kept her awake.
items.exampleCN: 太多咖啡因让她睡不着。

items.meaning: containing caffeine
items.example: He avoids caffeinated drinks after six.
items.exampleCN: 他六点以后不喝含咖啡因的饮料。

items.meaning: with the caffeine removed
items.example: She chose a decaffeinated coffee.
items.exampleCN: 她选了一杯低因咖啡。

definition_en: a flat piece of metal used as money, to invent a new word or phrase, or to make metal money
core_image: 拇指一弹，一枚亮闪闪的硬币在空中翻转
scene: 他在旧外套口袋里摸到一枚硬硬的小圆片。He found a coin under the sofa and laughed.
sceneCN: 这里 coin 指「硬币」（第 1 个义项：金属钱币）；句意是他在沙发下找到一枚硬币，笑了。

senses.title: A piece of metal money
senses.definition: a small flat piece of metal used as money
senses.definitionCN: 用作货币的小块扁金属
senses.example: He dropped a coin into the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一枚硬币投进机器。
senses.why: Metal stamped with a mark guaranteed its weight and value.
senses.whyCN: 在金属上压印标记，是为它的重量与价值作保。

senses.title: To invent a word
senses.definition: to invent a new word or phrase that others begin to use
senses.definitionCN: 创造别人开始使用的新词或说法
senses.example: The writer coined a phrase that everyone repeats.
senses.exampleCN: 那位作家造了一个人人重复的说法。
senses.why: A new word is struck like a coin: one face is form, the other meaning.
senses.whyCN: 新词像硬币一样被压出来：一面是形式，一面是意义。

senses.title: To mint metal money
senses.definition: to make coins from metal
senses.definitionCN: 用金属制造硬币
senses.example: The kingdom began to coin silver that year.
senses.exampleCN: 王国在那一年开始铸造银币。
senses.why: The verb came first in Latin, naming the stamping of metal.
senses.whyCN: 动词义在拉丁语中更早出现，本指在金属上压印。

intro.en: Coin comes from Latin cuneus, a wedge, because a wedge stamped the metal.
intro.cn: coin 出自拉丁语 cuneus（楔子），因为金属靠楔形模具压印。

items.en: Cuneus meant a wedge used to strike a die.
items.cn: cuneus 指压模时使用的楔子。

items.en: Moneta cuneata described money made by stamping.
items.cn: moneta cuneata 指压印而成的钱币。

items.en: Old French coin named the wedge-shaped die.
items.cn: 古法语 coin 指楔形模具。

items.en: English coin shifted from the die to the money itself.
items.cn: 英语 coin 从模具转指钱币本身。

items.en: Writers extended it to the striking of new words.
items.cn: 文人把它扩展到新词的锻造。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words that differ from coin by one letter, while the meaning group names money and the making of money.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 coin 只差一个字母的短词，近义组涉及钱与造钱。

entries.definition: a length of wire wound into rings
entries.definitionCN: 绕成圈的一段金属丝

entries.definition: the seed of grain plants such as wheat
entries.definitionCN: 小麦等谷物的籽粒

entries.definition: to become part of a group or activity
entries.definitionCN: 成为某个群体或活动的一部分

entries.definition: money in the form of notes and coins
entries.definitionCN: 纸币和硬币形式的钱

entries.definition: a round piece of metal used instead of money
entries.definitionCN: 代替钱币使用的圆形金属片

entries.definition: to make a coin from metal
entries.definitionCN: 用金属铸造硬币

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a stamped wedge, then move to small change and to a newly struck phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从压印的楔形模具出发，走到零钱与新造的说法。

normal.en: Coin and join differ by one letter, and a coin joins two faces.
normal.cn: coin 与 join 只差一个字母，一枚硬币把两面连在一起。

normal.en: The Latin base cuneus was a wedge, the tool that pressed the design.
normal.cn: 拉丁词基 cuneus 是楔子，正是压出图案的工具。

normal.en: Toss a coin and chance decides, a picture you can keep.
normal.cn: 抛一枚硬币让运气决定，这是一幅好记的画面。

normal.en: To coin a phrase is to strike a new word the way a mint strikes metal.
normal.cn: 造一个新说法，就像造币厂在金属上压出图案。

normal.en: Coinage covers both the money system and the words invented.
normal.cn: coinage 同时指货币制度与被造出的词语。

abstract.en: Picture a bright coin spinning on a wooden table until it falls flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚亮硬币在木桌上旋转，最后啪地落平。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy die coming down on a warm metal disc.
abstract.cn: 想象沉重的模具压在一块温热的金属圆片上。

abstract.en: Picture a poet writing two new words and watching them spread.
abstract.cn: 想象一位诗人写下两个新词，看着它们流传开。

examples.en: She put a coin in the old man's hand.
examples.cn: 她把一枚硬币放进老人手里。

examples.en: The scientist coined a term for the new material.
examples.cn: 科学家为这种新材料造了一个术语。

examples.en: That phrase was coined by a journalist in the last century.
examples.cn: 那个说法是上世纪一位记者造出来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 coin 记成一枚两面都有图案的硬币：一面是钱，一面是新词。

root: 源自拉丁语 cuneus（楔子），经古法语 coin 进入英语，由压印模具转为钱币，再引申为锻造新词。

sensesIntro.en: From the die that stamps metal to the money it makes, and then to words struck in the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 从压印金属的模具，到它造出的钱币，再到以同样方式锻造的词语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metal disc pressed by a die until a face appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：金属圆片被模具一压，图案浮现。

branches.en: The coin itself is the everyday sense of the noun.
branches.cn: 硬币本身是名词最日常的义项。

branches.en: A coined phrase is pressed out like a new piece of money.
branches.cn: 一个被造出的说法，就像一枚新压出的钱币。

branches.en: The verb keeps the old workshop act of striking metal.
branches.cn: 动词义保留了作坊里压印金属的古老动作。

branches.en: Both actions shape raw material into something accepted by others.
branches.cn: 两种动作都是把原材料塑成他人接受之物。

branches.en: Money and language both circulate once they are struck.
branches.cn: 钱币与词语一旦被压出，就开始流通。

intro.en: Coin forms a small family with -age, -er and a few compounds from daily trade.
intro.cn: coin 靠 -age、-er 以及日常交易中的少量复合词组成小家族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cuneus named a wedge and survives inside the history of coin, not as a living part.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cuneus 指楔子，只留在 coin 的历史里，已不是活成分。

items.meaning: more than one coin, or he makes metal money
items.example: The jar was full of small coins.
items.exampleCN: 罐子里装满了小硬币。

items.meaning: invented a word or made metal money
items.example: The term was coined in the nineteen twenties.
items.exampleCN: 这个术语是二十世纪二十年代造出的。

items.meaning: the act of inventing a word or making coins
items.example: Coining new words is common in science.
items.exampleCN: 在科学领域造新词很常见。

items.meaning: the system of coins or the words newly invented
items.example: The coinage of that era used pure silver.
items.exampleCN: 那个时期的钱币用纯银铸造。

items.meaning: a person who makes coins or invents words
items.example: The coiner of the slogan remained unknown.
items.exampleCN: 这个口号是谁造出来的仍无人知晓。

items.meaning: working only after a coin is put in
items.example: A coin-operated machine stood by the door.
items.exampleCN: 门边立着一台投币机器。

items.meaning: a small bag for carrying coins
items.example: Her coin purse held only a few pennies.
items.exampleCN: 她的硬币小包里只有几枚小钱。

items.meaning: the act of throwing a coin to decide something
items.example: The match began with a coin toss.
items.exampleCN: 比赛以抛硬币开始。

latinEntries.example: The Latin cuneus gives us the shape behind coin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 cuneus 提供了 coin 背后的形状。

definition_en: having a low temperature, showing little friendliness, or a common illness that blocks the nose and throat
core_image: 推开门时扑面而来的那股刺骨凉气
scene: 他忘了带手套，手指很快失去了知觉。The cold wind cut through her thin jacket.
sceneCN: 这里 cold 指「寒冷的」（第 1 个义项：温度低）；句意是寒风穿透了她单薄的外套。

senses.title: Having a low temperature
senses.definition: having a temperature much lower than the body
senses.definitionCN: 温度远低于体温的
senses.example: A cold wind blew across the empty field.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵冷风吹过空旷的田野。
senses.why: The oldest sense simply names the absence of warmth.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项只是命名温暖的缺席。

senses.title: Unfriendly in manner
senses.definition: showing no warm feeling towards other people
senses.definitionCN: 对他人不表现出温暖情感的
senses.example: Her cold reply ended the conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷淡的回答结束了谈话。
senses.why: Warmth became a picture for kindness, so its opposite became distance.
senses.whyCN: 温暖成了善意的比喻，它的反面便成了疏远。

senses.title: A common illness
senses.definition: a mild illness that makes you sneeze and blocks your nose
senses.definitionCN: 让人打喷嚏、鼻子不通的轻微疾病
senses.example: He caught a cold after walking home in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 他冒雨走回家后感冒了。
senses.why: Old medicine blamed a chill for the illness, and the name stayed.
senses.whyCN: 古代医学把这种病归咎于受寒，名字便留了下来。

intro.en: Cold is a native Germanic word, related to German kalt and Dutch koud.
intro.cn: cold 是日耳曼语本族词，与德语 kalt、荷兰语 koud 同源。

items.en: An old root described being frozen or chilly.
items.cn: 一个古老词根描述冻结或寒冷的状态。

items.en: The word cald named low temperature in everyday speech.
items.cn: cald 一词在日常语言中指低温。

items.en: The spelling settled as cold while the sense stayed physical.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 cold，词义仍是物理的冷。

items.en: Warmth became a metaphor, so cold could describe a person.
items.cn: 温暖成为比喻，于是 cold 可以形容人。

items.en: The noun also names the common illness of a blocked nose.
items.cn: 名词还指鼻子不通的常见小病。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that differ from cold by a letter, while the meaning group grades low temperature and names a related illness.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 cold 差一个字母的词，近义组区分低温程度并列出相关疾病。

entries.definition: a valuable yellow metal used for jewellery
entries.definitionCN: 用于首饰的贵重黄色金属

entries.definition: a thin rope or a piece of electrical wire
entries.definitionCN: 细绳或一段电线

entries.definition: brave and confident in a difficult situation
entries.definitionCN: 在困境中勇敢自信的

entries.definition: unpleasantly cool, but not freezing
entries.definitionCN: 凉得让人不舒服，但尚未结冰

entries.definition: extremely cold
entries.definitionCN: 极其寒冷

entries.definition: an illness like a cold but more severe
entries.definitionCN: 类似感冒但更严重的疾病

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the shiver of weather, the chill of a manner and the sneeze of a small illness.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子沿着天气的寒颤、态度的冷意与小病的喷嚏展开。

normal.en: Cold and gold differ by one letter, but only one of them warms your hand.
normal.cn: cold 与 gold 只差一个字母，但只有一个能暖手。

normal.en: The word is native English, so it looks like German kalt.
normal.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，所以与德语 kalt 长得很像。

normal.en: Warmth stands for kindness, so cold stands for distance.
normal.cn: 温暖代表善意，所以冷就代表疏远。

normal.en: You catch a cold, you do not catch the weather.
normal.cn: 人会说 catch a cold，但不会说 catch the weather。

normal.en: Colder and coldest simply add the regular endings.
normal.cn: colder 与 coldest 只是加了规则词尾。

abstract.en: Picture breath turning white at a frozen bus stop.
abstract.cn: 想象在冰冷的公交站，呼出的气变成白雾。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake refused and a face turned away.
abstract.cn: 想象一次被拒绝的握手和一张转开的脸。

abstract.en: Picture a pile of tissues beside a cup of hot tea.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯热茶旁边堆着用过的纸巾。

examples.en: The water in the bucket was cold and clear.
examples.cn: 桶里的水又冷又清。

examples.en: He gave me a cold look and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他冷冷地看了我一眼，什么也没说。

examples.en: She stayed home because she had a bad cold.
examples.cn: 她因为重感冒而待在家里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cold 记成推门时扑面的一股凉气：凉了身体，也凉了态度。

root: 日耳曼语本族词，古英语作 cald，与德语 kalt 同源，由低温引申为态度冷淡与感冒。

sensesIntro.en: From the temperature of air to the temperature of a manner, and then to the illness a chill brings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从空气的温度，到态度的温度，再到受寒引起的疾病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gust of frosty air striking an uncovered face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股带霜气的风扑在毫无遮挡的脸上。

branches.en: The physical sense is the root of the whole family.
branches.cn: 物理的冷是整个词族的根。

branches.en: A cold manner borrows the feeling of cold air.
branches.cn: 冷淡的态度借用了冷空气带来的感觉。

branches.en: The illness keeps an old link between a chill and sickness.
branches.cn: 感冒义保留了受寒与生病之间的古老联系。

branches.en: Both senses measure a lack of warmth.
branches.cn: 两个义项衡量的都是温暖的缺失。

branches.en: Cold air and the common cold share one name in many languages.
branches.cn: 在许多语言里，冷空气与感冒共用一个名字。

intro.en: Cold takes the regular endings for comparison and builds many compounds with -ness and with body words.
intro.cn: cold 接规则比较词尾，并与 -ness 及身体词构成许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here; the word belongs to the Germanic layer of English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分，这个词属于英语的日耳曼语层。

items.meaning: having a lower temperature
items.example: The night grew colder after midnight.
items.exampleCN: 午夜以后夜变得更冷。

items.meaning: having the lowest temperature
items.example: This is the coldest room in the house.
items.exampleCN: 这是屋里最冷的房间。

items.meaning: more than one case of the illness
items.example: Children get colds several times a year.
items.exampleCN: 孩子一年会感冒好几次。

items.meaning: in an unfriendly way
items.example: He answered coldly and left the room.
items.exampleCN: 他冷淡地回答后离开了房间。

items.meaning: the state of being cold or unfriendly
items.example: The coldness in her voice surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 她声音里的冷淡让我们吃惊。

items.meaning: having a body temperature that changes with the air
items.example: Lizards are cold-blooded animals.
items.exampleCN: 蜥蜴是冷血动物。

items.meaning: as cold as ice
items.example: He drank a glass of ice-cold water.
items.exampleCN: 他喝了一杯冰水。

items.meaning: showing no sympathy for others
items.example: Refusing help seemed cold-hearted.
items.exampleCN: 拒绝帮助显得冷酷无情。

definition_en: to fall down suddenly, to fail completely, or to fall down because of illness or weakness
core_image: 一座楼在几秒之内塌成一堆瓦砾
scene: 旧仓库的屋顶在雨里撑不住了。The old roof collapsed under the weight of snow.
sceneCN: 这里 collapse 指「倒塌」（第 1 个义项：突然塌下）；句意是旧屋顶在积雪的重压下塌了。

senses.title: Fall down suddenly
senses.definition: to fall down suddenly because of pressure or a loss of support
senses.definitionCN: 因压力或失去支撑而突然塌下
senses.example: The roof collapsed under the weight of snow.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶在积雪的重压下塌了。
senses.why: The Latin base meant to fall together, which is exactly what a building does.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为一起倒下，这正是一栋楼倒塌的样子。

senses.title: Fail completely
senses.definition: to fail suddenly and completely, as a system or a plan does
senses.definitionCN: 像制度或计划那样突然彻底失败
senses.example: The talks collapsed after two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈两小时后破裂了。
senses.why: An argument can fall down like a wall when its supports give way.
senses.whyCN: 论证的支撑一断，也会像墙一样倒下。

senses.title: Fall down from weakness
senses.definition: to fall down suddenly because of illness, injury or tiredness
senses.definitionCN: 因病、受伤或疲劳突然倒下
senses.example: He collapsed at the end of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 他在比赛终点倒下了。
senses.why: The body loses its support just as a structure does.
senses.whyCN: 身体像建筑物一样失去支撑。

intro.en: Collapse comes from Latin collabi, from com- together and labi, to slip or fall.
intro.cn: collapse 出自拉丁语 collabi，由 com-（一起）与 labi（滑落、倒下）组成。

items.en: Labi meant to slip, slide or fall.
items.cn: labi 意为滑、滑落或倒下。

items.en: Collabi described falling down in a heap.
items.cn: collabi 描述塌成一堆。

items.en: The participle collapsus was used of ruined buildings.
items.cn: 分词 collapsus 用于描述毁坏的建筑。

items.en: English collapse first described a building giving way.
items.cn: 英语 collapse 最初描述建筑垮塌。

items.en: Medicine and economics extended it to bodies and systems.
items.cn: 医学与经济学把它扩展到身体与制度。

note.en: The look-alike group holds Latin-shaped words with similar endings, while the meaning group names ways of breaking down or losing strength.
note.cn: 形近组收的是结尾相似、带拉丁形态的词，近义组列出碎裂与失去支撑的说法。

entries.definition: to pass, as time does
entries.definitionCN: 像时间那样流逝

entries.definition: to gather pages into the correct order
entries.definitionCN: 把书页按正确顺序整理

entries.definition: the hiding of the sun or moon by another body
entries.definitionCN: 太阳或月亮被另一天体遮住

entries.definition: to break into small pieces over time
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐碎成小块

entries.definition: to go down below a surface
entries.definitionCN: 沉到表面以下

entries.definition: to lose consciousness for a short time
entries.definitionCN: 短时间失去知觉

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the Latin picture of falling together, then apply it to walls, plans and bodies.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一起倒下的拉丁画面出发，再挪到墙、计划与身体上。

normal.en: Collapse hides the Latin verb labi, to slip, so the word pictures a slide downward.
normal.cn: collapse 里藏着拉丁动词 labi（滑落），画面就是往下滑。

normal.en: The prefix com- means together, so everything falls at once.
normal.cn: 前缀 com- 意为一起，所以是所有东西同时倒下。

normal.en: A roof, a deal and a runner can all collapse in one second.
normal.cn: 屋顶、交易和奔跑者都可能在刹那间垮掉。

normal.en: Add -ible and collapsible means able to be folded down.
normal.cn: 加上 -ible，collapsible 就是能被折下来的。

normal.en: The noun keeps the same shape as the verb, so no ending is needed.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，不必另加词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a wall folding inward in a cloud of dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙在尘土中向内折倒。

abstract.en: Picture a row of numbers on a screen suddenly turning blank.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上的一排数字突然变成空白。

abstract.en: Picture a runner taking one more step and then folding to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象奔跑者又迈一步，然后蜷倒在地。

examples.en: The bridge collapsed during the storm.
examples.cn: 那座桥在暴风雨中坍塌了。

examples.en: The company collapsed after losing its main investor.
examples.cn: 这家公司在失去主要投资人后垮掉了。

examples.en: She collapsed with tiredness after the long flight.
examples.cn: 长途飞行后她累得倒下了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collapse 记成 com 加 lapse：所有东西一起滑落，就是塌掉。

root: 源自拉丁语 collabi，com-（一起）加 labi（滑落），本指建筑塌成一堆，后引申为制度失败与身体倒下。

sensesIntro.en: From a roof falling in to a plan breaking down, and then to a body that can no longer stand.
sensesIntro.cn: 从屋顶塌下，到计划破裂，再到再也站不住的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a structure losing its support and folding into a heap.
core.cn: 核心意象：结构失去支撑，折成一堆。

branches.en: The building sense is the oldest and most physical.
branches.cn: 建筑义最古老，也最具体。

branches.en: A plan fails the way a wall gives way.
branches.cn: 计划失败，就像墙失去支撑。

branches.en: The body sense borrows the same loss of support.
branches.cn: 身体义借用的同样是支撑的丧失。

branches.en: Both a roof and a person can fall in one sudden movement.
branches.cn: 屋顶和人都会在一个突然的动作中倒下。

branches.en: Systems and bodies both need support to keep standing.
branches.cn: 制度与身体都需要支撑才能立住。

intro.en: Collapse belongs to the Latin labi family, which also gives lapse, elapse and relapse.
intro.cn: collapse 属于拉丁语 labi 词族，这一族还给出 lapse、elapse 与 relapse。

latinIntro.en: The base labi, to slip, is the living element behind the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 labi（滑落）是整组词背后活的成分。

items.meaning: more than one collapse, or it falls down
items.example: The old wall collapses in heavy rain.
items.exampleCN: 这堵旧墙在大雨中塌下。

items.meaning: fell down or failed completely
items.example: The tent collapsed in the wind.
items.exampleCN: 帐篷在风里塌了。

items.meaning: falling down at this moment
items.example: They fled the collapsing building.
items.exampleCN: 他们逃离了正在倒塌的建筑。

items.meaning: able to be folded or pushed down
items.example: She carried a collapsible cup.
items.exampleCN: 她带着一只可折叠的杯子。

items.meaning: a small failure or a passing of time
items.example: A lapse in attention caused the error.
items.exampleCN: 一次走神造成了这个错误。

items.meaning: of time, to pass by
items.example: Three hours elapsed before the call came.
items.exampleCN: 三个小时过去，电话才来。

items.meaning: to fall back into illness or a bad habit
items.example: He relapsed after a week of rest.
items.exampleCN: 休息一周后他又复发了。

items.meaning: a body part slipping out of place
items.example: The doctor treated a minor prolapse.
items.exampleCN: 医生治疗了一处轻微的脱垂。

latinEntries.example: Latin collabi is built from com- and labi.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 collabi 由 com- 与 labi 构成。

latinEntries.example: The verb labi also lies behind relapse.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 动词 labi 也藏在 relapse 背后。

definition_zh: 衣领；领子；项圈；环状物；抓住某人；给…戴上项圈；扭住
definition_en: the part of a shirt, coat, or dress that fits around the neck, or a band put around an animal's neck; as a verb, to seize someone by the collar or catch someone
core_image: 脖子上的那一圈：衣服收拢脖颈的边缘，或套在动物颈上的环带
scene: 小狗在院子里飞奔，主人举起一根红绳子，说：He bent down to fasten the collar around the dog's neck before their evening walk.
sceneCN: 这里 collar 是「项圈」（第 3 个义项：套在动物颈部的环带）；句意是遛狗前主人弯腰给狗扣好项圈，画面聚焦在脖子上那一圈东西。

pos.zh: 衣领；领子；项圈；环状物；柱头
抓住某人的领口；扭住；截住（某人说话）；给…戴上项圈

derivatives.zh: 由名词加形容词化用法构成，义为「有领子的」「被捉住的」
由 collar 构成的复合形容词，义为「白领的，从事脑力劳动的」
由 collar 构成的复合形容词，义为「蓝领的，从事体力劳动的」

senses.title: The neck part of a garment
senses.definition: the folded part of a shirt, coat, or dress that fits around the neck
senses.definitionCN: 衬衫、外套或连衣裙中围住颈部的部分
senses.example: He turned up his coat collar against the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 他竖起大衣领子挡风。
senses.why: The neck is where a garment gathers and closes, so the encircling edge becomes the word's first image.
senses.whyCN: 颈部是衣服收拢、闭合的位置，围合脖子的边缘自然成为这个词最早的核心意象。

senses.title: A band for identification or restraint around a neck
senses.definition: a band worn around the neck, such as a pet's collar or a marked band
senses.definitionCN: 戴在颈部的环带，如宠物项圈或标识环
senses.example: The bird was fitted with a numbered plastic collar.
senses.exampleCN: 这只鸟被套上了带编号的塑料颈环。
senses.why: Anything that encircles the neck shares the collar shape, so the image extends from clothing to bands.
senses.whyCN: 凡是围住颈部的环形物都与衣领形状相同，意象从衣服自然延伸到环带。

senses.title: A collar for an animal
senses.definition: a leather or fabric band fastened around a dog or other animal's neck, often holding a tag or leash
senses.definitionCN: 拴在狗或其他动物颈部的皮带或布带，常挂标签或牵引绳
senses.example: She bought a red collar with a small bell for her cat.
senses.exampleCN: 她给猫买了一个挂小铃铛的红色项圈。
senses.why: Sense 02 narrows to animals: the band becomes a tool for controlling and identifying the pet.
senses.whyCN: 由第 02 义项收窄到动物：环带从装饰变为控制和辨认宠物的工具。

senses.title: A ring-shaped part of a machine
senses.definition: a ring or flange on a shaft, pipe, or machine part that holds something in place
senses.definitionCN: 轴、管或机械零件上的环形或凸缘部件，用于定位固定
senses.example: A steel collar keeps the wheel fixed on the axle.
senses.exampleCN: 一个钢制轴环把车轮固定在轴上。
senses.why: Machines use collars to clamp round parts, reusing the encircling image in an engineering sense.
senses.whyCN: 机械用环箍住圆形部件，「围合」意象在工程领域得到复用。

senses.title: To seize someone by the collar
senses.definition: to grab a person by the neck or collar of clothing, especially to stop or hold them
senses.definitionCN: 抓住某人的颈部或衣领，尤指为了拦住或控制对方
senses.example: The guard collared the boy who tried to sneak in.
senses.exampleCN: 保安扭住了那个想溜进去的男孩。
senses.why: The noun names the grabbing point at the neck; turning it into a verb makes the collar the handle of arrest.
senses.whyCN: 名词标记的是颈部的抓握点；名词转动词后，衣领成了捉人的把手。

senses.title: To stop and talk to someone
senses.definition: to catch someone and make them listen or talk, often when they are in a hurry
senses.definitionCN: 拦住某人使其听自己说话，常指对方正赶时间时
senses.example: I got collared by my neighbor in the hallway and heard her whole story.
senses.exampleCN: 我在楼道里被邻居截住，听她讲了半天。
senses.why: Metaphorically grabbing a person's collar to detain them extends physical seizure into social interception.
senses.whyCN: 把「抓住衣领」的物理动作隐喻为「拦下说话」，捉拿意象延伸到社交场合。

senses.title: To put a collar on an animal
senses.definition: to fasten a collar around an animal's neck
senses.definitionCN: 给动物颈部扣上项圈
senses.example: All dogs in the park must be collared and tagged.
senses.exampleCN: 公园里所有的狗都必须戴上项圈并挂牌。
senses.why: The animal collar of sense 03 becomes an action: fitting the band is routine care and legal duty.
senses.whyCN: 第 03 义项的动物项圈转为动作：戴上项圈成为日常照料与规范要求。

senses.title: White-collar and blue-collar social labels
senses.definition: used in compounds to classify workers by the color of shirt they traditionally wore
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词，按传统衬衫领色划分劳动者类型
senses.example: White-collar jobs usually happen in offices, not on factory floors.
senses.exampleCN: 白领工作通常在办公室进行，而不是在车间。
senses.why: The visible part of a work shirt, its collar, becomes a metonymy for whole classes of workers.
senses.whyCN: 工作衬衫最显眼的部分——衣领——借代为整个劳动者阶层的标签。

intro.en: Collar goes back through Old French coler to Latin collum, the neck, so the word has always named what encircles the neck.
intro.cn: collar 经古法语 coler 上溯至拉丁语 collum（颈、脖），这个词从一开始就指「围住颈部的东西」。

items.en: A root usually reconstructed as *kwolh₁- or related *kwel-, meaning to turn or revolve, giving roundness as a core idea.
items.cn: 一般认为源自重构词根 *kwolh₁-（与 *kwel- 相关），意为「转动、旋转」，由此带来「圆形、环状」的核心概念。

items.en: Collum meant the neck, the body part that connects head and shoulders; derivatives like collare (neckband) already pointed to things worn there.
items.cn: 拉丁语 collum 意为「颈部」，即连接头与肩的部位；其派生词 collare（颈带）已指戴在颈上的东西。

items.en: Coler or colier meant the neck of a garment and also a neckband, passing into English after the Norman Conquest.
items.cn: 古法语 coler／colier 指衣服的领部及颈带，随诺曼征服进入英语。

items.en: First attested in Middle English around 1300 as the neck part of a garment, the everyday clothing sense.
items.cn: 中古英语约 1300 年首次见于记载，指衣服的领部，即日常衣着义。

items.en: The verb senses of seizing by the collar and detaining someone developed from the noun image.
items.cn: 16 至 17 世纪，由名词意象发展出「抓住领口」「拦住某人」等动词义。

items.en: Industrial and social extensions appeared: machine collars, and the white-collar versus blue-collar class labels of the late 19th and 20th centuries.
items.cn: 近现代出现工程与社会的延伸：机械轴环，以及 19 世纪末以来「白领／蓝领」的阶层标签。

note.en: Words that look or sound like collar, and words close to its neck-related meaning.
note.cn: 与 collar 形近音近的词，以及意义相关的「颈部、环带、抓住」类词。

entries.definition: the Latin word for neck, the direct ancestor of collar
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「颈部」，collar 的直接来源

entries.definition: anger or irritability, from the old idea of yellow bile; only sounds identical to collar, unrelated origin
entries.definitionCN: 愤怒、易怒，源自「黄胆汁」的古观念；与 collar 仅发音相同，词源无关

entries.definition: the visual property of objects; one letter different from collar and a different root
entries.definitionCN: 颜色，与 collar 仅一字母之差，词源不同

entries.definition: to fall down or break down suddenly; begins with coll- but comes from Latin labi, to slip
entries.definitionCN: 倒塌、崩溃，词首同为 coll-，但源自拉丁语 labi（滑落），并非同根

entries.definition: a band worn around the neck, close to collar senses 02 and 03
entries.definitionCN: 颈带、围颈的带子，接近 collar 的环带义

entries.definition: a strap fastened to a dog's collar to control it
entries.definitionCN: 拴狗绳，与项圈配套使用的控制带

entries.definition: to take hold of suddenly and forcefully, as in seizing someone by the collar
entries.definitionCN: 猛然抓住，用于「抓住领口」的对应动作

normalIntro.en: Build the word from its Latin root and its everyday images.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁词根和日常画面入手记住这个词。

normal.en: Latin collum means neck; anything around the neck can be a collar.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 collum 意为「颈部」；凡围在颈上的东西都可称 collar。

normal.en: Old French coler kept the same neck meaning and handed it to English.
normal.cn: 古法语 coler 沿用「颈部」义，将其传入英语。

normal.en: White collar versus blue collar: office shirts versus work shirts.
normal.cn: 白领对蓝领：办公衬衫对工装衬衫，领色区分阶层。

normal.en: Collocation habit: fasten a collar, turn up a collar, seize by the collar.
normal.cn: 搭配习惯：扣项圈、竖领子、抓领口。

normal.en: The verb sense: to collar someone is to grab them by that neck band.
normal.cn: 动词义：to collar someone 就是揪住对方那圈领子。

abstract.en: Picture a circle closing around a neck: cloth, leather, steel, all the same ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈东西在颈上闭合：布、皮革、钢铁，都是同一个环。

abstract.en: The collar is the handle by which the world grabs you or you grab it.
abstract.cn: 领子是被世界抓住、或你抓住世界的把手。

abstract.en: A collar marks belonging: pet to owner, worker to class, wheel to axle.
abstract.cn: 环带标记归属：宠物之于主人、工人之于阶层、车轮之于车轴。

examples.en: He turned up his coat collar against the cold wind.
examples.cn: 他竖起大衣领子抵御寒风。

examples.en: Remember to fasten the collar on your dog before the walk.
examples.cn: 遛狗前记得给你的狗扣好项圈。

examples.en: White-collar workers spend most of the day in offices.
examples.cn: 白领工作者一天中大部分时间都在办公室度过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「磕了」——小狗脖子上的项圈一磕到地就响了，一「磕了」就想起 collar 是那圈环带。

root: 源自拉丁语 collum（颈、脖），经古法语 coler／colier 进入英语。核心意象是「围住颈部的环形物」：衣领、项圈、轴环皆由此延伸，动词义「抓住领口」「截住某人」由名词意象转喻而来。

sensesIntro.en: From the garment collar at the neck, the word widens to any encircling band, narrows to animal collars and machine rings, and turns verbal for grabbing and detaining.
sensesIntro.cn: 从颈部的衣领出发，词义扩展到各种环带，再收窄到动物项圈与机械轴环，并转为动词表示抓握与拦人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring that encircles the neck, whether of cloth, leather, or steel
core.cn: 核心意象：围住颈部的环，无论是布料、皮革还是钢铁

branches.en: the garment edge at the neck
branches.cn: 颈部衣服的边缘：衣领本义

branches.en: bands worn around necks, especially animal collars
branches.cn: 围颈的环带，尤其是动物项圈

branches.en: engineering rings that clamp round parts
branches.cn: 工程上箍住圆形部件的轴环

branches.en: grabbing or stopping a person by the collar image
branches.cn: 借「抓领口」意象表示捉住或拦住某人

branches.en: fitting collars and the white-collar social label
branches.cn: 戴上项圈的动作，以及白领蓝领的社会标签

intro.en: Collar itself carries no prefix or suffix, but its family and compounds show how the neck image spreads.
intro.cn: collar 本身不带前后缀，但其词族与复合词显示了「颈部」意象的扩散。

latinIntro.en: Latin collum, the neck, generated a family of neck-related words in Romance languages and scientific Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 collum（颈）在罗曼语族与科学拉丁语中生成了一系列与颈相关的词族。

items.meaning: neck
items.example: A collar encircles the coll-, the neck.
items.exampleCN: collar 就是围住颈部的环带。

items.meaning: the neck
items.example: Anatomists still use collum for necklike parts.
items.exampleCN: 解剖学中仍用 collum 指颈状结构。

items.meaning: without a collar
items.example: He wore a collarless shirt on holiday.
items.exampleCN: 度假时他穿无领衬衫。

items.meaning: having a collar, or caught
items.example: The collared dove is a common garden bird.
items.exampleCN: 灰斑鸠是庭园里常见的鸟。

items.meaning: of office workers
items.example: White-collar crime is committed in offices.
items.exampleCN: 白领犯罪发生在办公室里。

items.meaning: of manual workers
items.example: Blue-collar neighborhoods grew around the factory.
items.exampleCN: 蓝领社区围绕工厂发展起来。

items.meaning: a band on a dog's neck
items.example: The dog collar carried the owner's phone number.
items.exampleCN: 狗项圈上挂着主人的电话号码。

items.meaning: the clavicle, bone near the neck base
items.example: He cracked his collarbone in the fall.
items.exampleCN: 他摔倒时摔裂了锁骨。

items.meaning: a clothing set or an orthopedic sling
items.meaningCN: 衣领与袖口；颈腕悬吊带

latinEntries.exampleCN: 解剖学用 collum cervicale 指颈段。

latinEntries.exampleCN: vertebrae collaris 指颈椎。
